publicReleaseNotes: Penny 0.2.0 restores older backups: rer import, before setup, places a backup made by an earlier Penny in this installation's migration history, replays the later triage settings and status-clock rows, and keeps notification history through the merge-notice rebuild, with every archived row and original file exact on native and RER Managed destinations. Releases and roadmap status updates can be scheduled for a workspace-local time and are published once by Cron after the same checks as Publish now (REL-014). Overview shows loop health with drilldowns to the counted records (MEAS-006). The owner chooses the AI provider and model per capability, a monthly USD cap and the private-data setting; AI work reserves its cost before a call and reports metered cost after, and private notes and commercial fields stay out of prompts by default (AI-010). The release also carries the ownership, internal-discussion, demand-attribution and no-mail-loop clause landings since 0.1.4. Migrations 0086 and 0087 are additive. It runs on rer 0.2.76. SendGrid duplicate suppression, live external feedback providers and whole-product acceptance beyond the proved core loop remain known limits. Product screenshot: public/brand/releases/penny-0.2.0-1440.png

DOCS-001.summary: Clarify public documentation wording, current delivery boundary and acceptance evidence.
DOCS-001.was: The public paths `/docs` and `/docs/<slug>` serve Penny's first-party documentation: the Markdown files that `docs/site.json` lists as published, in the sections and order it gives, which is the only navigation. The Markdown is rendered to HTML at build time by a Vite plugin, in a build and in development, and never in the Worker or the browser; each page is its own lazily loaded chunk that the Worker renders per request. A page has its title as its one top-level heading, under the same header as the product landing (HOME-002): Penny's coin mark and name linking to `/`, then links to the docs (marked as the current section), the public board at `/portal`, the source repository and `/signin`, of which a phone keeps the mark, the name and sign-in; the landing's footer repeats them. It has a section menu, an on-this-page list, previous and next links, tables in labelled scrollable regions and an Edit-on-GitHub link; after the page loads, moving between docs pages is client-side navigation. Every Markdown file at the repository root, under `docs/` and as a top-level `<directory>/README.md` is either published or listed in the manifest as GitHub-only with a reason, and an unlisted file fails verification. A broken internal link or anchor, an image outside `docs/media/` or an absolute build-machine path fails the build; raw HTML in the Markdown is shown as text, never rendered. The documentation reads no workspace record, requester or operator identity or session, sets no cookie and loads only same-origin resources. An unknown or nested slug answers a `404` with no article.

OPS-004.summary: Clarify global search wording, current delivery boundary and acceptance evidence.
OPS-004.was: Operators can search request titles and descriptions, evidence wording, decision questions and rationales, roadmap item titles and summaries, release titles and bodies, requester display names and email addresses, and account names. The first page of results returns within 500ms.
OPS-004.now: Operators can search request titles and descriptions, evidence wording, decision questions and rationales, roadmap item titles and summaries, release titles and bodies, requester display names and email addresses, account names, and product, component and feature names (PRIO-001). Product, component and feature results pass the same permission filtering as every other searched record, so an operator never sees a name they cannot open, and rank in the same order as the other results. The first page of results returns within 500ms. Search across every other named field ships; product, component and feature names are not yet searched (`src/core/features/workspace/list-repository.ts`), and the 500ms first page at declared capacity is not load-tested. *Acceptance:* Searching one product, one component and one feature, each by its full name and by a partial name, returns it with a link to its record and in the same ranking as other results; an operator who cannot open it does not see it.

ROLE-001.summary: Clarify custom roles and restricted commercial fields wording, current delivery boundary and acceptance evidence.
ROLE-001.was: Admins define custom roles from a fixed permission set (capture evidence and proxy votes, moderate, publish, commit decisions, manage roadmap, manage releases, manage integrations, manage automation, view commercial fields, export, erase) and assign them to operators. Commercial fields (revenue, MRR/ARR, opportunity amounts, health) are hidden from roles without "view commercial fields" in every screen, API response, export, agent answer and notification. *Acceptance:* A base test signs in under a role without commercial permission and reads requests, accounts, prioritisation views, CSV exports and Ask Penny answers through their routes: no revenue, opportunity or health value appears; granting the permission reveals them on the next request; each role change is in the audit log (ROLE-004).

ROLE-004.summary: Clarify audit log wording, current delivery boundary and acceptance evidence.
ROLE-004.was: Owners and Admins read, filter (actor, action, subject, date) and export as CSV or JSON an audit log of every privileged action: publication, moderation verdict, edit, removal, restore and permanent delete of published content (REQ-038), branding and sender changes (INT-007, NOTIFY-013), merge and unmerge, commitment, role and member change, integration connect and disconnect, automation rule change, export, erasure and every agent action, with the person or agent responsible. CAP-009.summary: Clarify email capture wording, current delivery boundary and acceptance evidence.
CAP-009.was: Each installation has a dedicated capture address on the owner's domain (Cloudflare Email Routing or the configured mail provider's inbound parse). Operators forward or BCC customer emails to it. Penny accepts only mail from operator addresses or allowlisted domains with DMARC alignment, recovers the original sender from the forwarded message, keeps attachments within `seed.json` limits and creates one inbox item per message ID. Notification reply addresses never reach this route (NOTIFY-004). *Acceptance:* Inbound-mail fixtures: forwarded Gmail and Outlook messages each create one item attributed to the original sender; a replayed message ID, an unaligned sender and a reply to a Penny notification create nothing.
CAP-009.now: Each installation has a dedicated capture address on the owner's domain (Cloudflare Email Routing or the configured mail provider's inbound parse). Operators forward or BCC customer emails to it. Penny accepts only mail from operator addresses or allowlisted domains with DMARC alignment, recovers the original sender from the forwarded message, keeps attachments within `seed.json` limits and creates one inbox item per message ID. Notification reply addresses never reach this route, and it refuses mail from Penny's own sender addresses (`MAIL_FROM` and any NOTIFY-013 sender), as NOTIFY-004 requires. *Acceptance:* Inbound-mail fixtures: forwarded Gmail and Outlook messages each create one item attributed to the original sender; a replayed message ID, an unaligned sender, mail from Penny's own sender address and a reply to a Penny notification create nothing.

WIDGET-001.summary: Clarify in-app feedback widget wording, current delivery boundary and acceptance evidence.
WIDGET-001.was: A JavaScript snippet and npm package embed Penny in the customer's own product as a launcher, modal or side panel: identified users submit, search, vote, comment and follow without leaving the product, and the current page URL and any metadata the host passes are attached as private context. It loads only from the installation's origin, sets no third-party cookie, follows the board's moderation setting (REQ-003, REQ-033) so an identified user's post on an auto-publish board shows at once, keeps the portal's privacy, and shows the owner's brand (INT-007) in the host's colours or the brand accent, as the owner chooses. Allow-listed iframe embedding of the portal (REQ-027) ships today. *Acceptance:* A browser test on a fixture host page at both widths: an identified user submits, votes and follows, and on an auto-publish board sees their post listed at once; the page URL appears only in private evidence; the documented CSP directives suffice; no third-party cookie is set.

AI-001.summary: Clarify semantic duplicate detection wording, current delivery boundary and acceptance evidence.
AI-001.was: Alongside EVID-007's lexical suggestions, Penny ranks existing requests by meaning (embeddings over titles, descriptions and linked evidence) for a requester typing a title, for each inbox item and for an operator viewing a request, and names the passages that matched. Requesters see published requests only. When the model is unavailable the lexical suggestions still appear. *Acceptance:* `pnpm run eval:ai -- --set duplicates-v1` (AI-011) over the repository's labelled pair set reports, at the suggestion threshold, precision of at least 0.90 and recall of at least 0.85, the true duplicate among the top five suggestions for at least 0.90 of positive pairs, and recall on the paraphrase subset at least 0.15 above the lexical EVID-007 baseline measured on the same set; requester suggestions contain only published requests; with the model disabled, lexical suggestions still return within EVID-007's limit.

When the model is unavailable the lexical suggestions still appear. *Acceptance:* `pnpm run eval:ai -- --set duplicates-v1` (AI-011) over the repository's labeled pair set reports, at the suggestion threshold, precision of at least 0.90 and recall of at least 0.85, the true duplicate among the top five suggestions for at least 0.90 of positive pairs, and recall on the paraphrase subset at least 0.15 above the lexical EVID-007 baseline measured on the same set; requester suggestions contain only published requests; with the model disabled, lexical suggestions still return within EVID-007's limit.

AI-002.summary: Clarify auto-link suggestions wording, current delivery boundary and acceptance evidence.
AI-002.was: Each new inbox item gets up to three suggested requests and one suggested theme, each with a confidence and a reason; the operator accepts or rejects in one action, and a rejected suggestion is not offered again. An owner may enable a rule that links automatically above a confidence threshold for chosen sources; auto-links are marked, reversible, and never publish, vote or notify. *Acceptance:* `pnpm run eval:ai -- --set links-v1` (AI-011) reports the labelled request among the three suggestions for at least 0.85 of items that have one, no suggestion above the threshold for at least 0.80 of items labelled none, and auto-link precision of at least 0.97 at the default threshold; an inbox journey accepts and rejects suggestions; an auto-link rule on one fixture source links only above its threshold, marks and can undo each link, and changes no public payload.

AI-005.summary: Clarify themes and adaptive taxonomy wording, current delivery boundary and acceptance evidence.
AI-005.was: Penny keeps a hierarchical taxonomy (area, theme, sub-theme) over all evidence and requests, classifies new feedback continuously, proposes new themes as volume emerges, and lets operators rename, merge, split, pin or retire themes; operator edits win and reclassification keeps history. Themes filter every list and appear in reports (MEAS-004). *Acceptance:* `pnpm run eval:ai -- --set themes-v1` (AI-011) reports agreement with the adjudicated labels of macro-F1 at least 0.80 at area and theme level and at least 0.70 at sub-theme level, and Cohen's kappa at least 90% of the recorded agreement between the two human labellers; a fixture corpus gets an initial taxonomy; new feedback is classified in the next run; an operator split reclassifies with history; themes filter the inbox and the request queue.

AI-010.summary: The owner chooses the provider and model per AI capability, a monthly USD cap with reserved and metered cost, and whether private context may reach a model (off by default).
AI-010.was: The owner chooses the model provider and model for each AI capability (default: Claude through the Base AI module), a monthly USD budget and data-processing settings. Every AI run reserves and reports cost as LEARN-006 does; an absent or exhausted model visibly refuses AI work while every non-AI path keeps working. LEARN-006's configuration and cost reservation ship today for learning runs. *Acceptance:* Exhausting a fixture budget refuses new AI runs with a visible reason while lexical suggestions, manual capture and triage keep working; the cost report matches metered fixture usage.

Every AI run reserves and reports cost as LEARN-006 does; an absent or exhausted model visibly refuses AI work while every non-AI path keeps working. Settings choose OpenAI or Anthropic and a catalog model per capability, a UTC-calendar-month USD cap (initially $0), and whether permitted private context may be sent. AI-011.summary: Clarify measured ai quality wording, current delivery boundary and acceptance evidence.
AI-011.was: Every AI capability that suggests, links, merges, classifies, extracts, flags or redacts is measured against a named, versioned, labelled fixture set held in the repository under `tests/fixtures/ai/`: `duplicates-v1` (at least 300 request pairs, at least 30% of them hard negatives that share key terms but differ in need, and paraphrase positives with no shared terms), `links-v1` (at least 200 inbox items labelled with their request or none, and their theme), `merges-v1` (a backlog of at least 500 requests across at least three boards with labelled duplicate clusters), `extraction-v1` (at least 50 tickets, calls, emails and threads with labelled request spans), `themes-v1` (at least 400 items with a three-level taxonomy labelled by two people and adjudicated, with their agreement recorded), `spam-v1` (at least 300 submissions and comments labelled spam, abuse, personal data or clean) and `redaction-v1` (at least 200 excerpts with labelled sensitive spans). `pnpm run eval:ai -- --set <name> [--model <id>]` runs a capability over its set through the configured model adapter and writes a report naming the set version and hash, model and prompt version, counts, precision, recall, F1 or agreement, the confusion matrix and cost, and whether each bar in ACCEPTANCE.md's "AI quality bars" table is met; it exits non-zero when one is not. The lexical baseline (EVID-007) is evaluated on `duplicates-v1` without a model, so every report has a floor to beat. Each model evaluation is recorded as a dated receipt in ACCEPTANCE.md. In the product, settings show the latest evaluation for the configured model on each capability, and an auto-link (AI-002), auto-merge (AI-003), automatic theme assignment (AI-005) or automatic request creation (AI-004) rule cannot be enabled for a model and prompt version whose recorded evaluation is missing or below its bar; changing either one turns such rules off until a passing evaluation is recorded. Operators' accept and reject decisions can be exported as a private labelled set to run the same evaluation on the owner's own data; it is never committed to the repository. *Acceptance:* Each named set exists with its documented size and label mix; the evaluation command reports every figure above for each set and exits non-zero on a deliberately degraded fixture model; the lexical baseline run needs no model; enabling auto-merge for a model with no passing evaluation is refused with the reason, and a passing evaluation allows it.

REQ-040.summary: Clarify board participation and display settings wording, current delivery boundary and acceptance evidence.
REQ-040.was: Each public board has settings, as Canny's board settings do: who may post (requesters, or operators only, which makes a vote-and-comment board on which the portal and widget offer no submit form and an API or widget submission is refused with 403), whether requester comments are allowed, whether vote totals show publicly (when hidden, vote totals leave every public read and the API, the board may still sort by them, and operators still see them), whether voters' display names are listed publicly on a request (off by default; when on, the vote control states it before voting), and whether requester names show publicly or every requester reads as "Anonymous" (operators always see who). A setting change applies to every public read within 5 seconds and removes no record. For Canny migration (MIG-001), only the board visibility (`isPrivate`) and historical comment visibility (`privateComments`) exposed by [Canny’s API reference](https://developers.canny.io/api-reference) are mapped automatically. Posting permission, vote-count visibility, voter visibility and anonymity are not exposed by that API. For each board, the migration shows a reviewed board-settings mapping for those four settings, with the Canny dashboard values entered or confirmed by the owner before apply. Requester comment participation is also an explicit owner choice: `privateComments` governs historical comment visibility, not permission to comment. The preview distinguishes source API fields from owner-confirmed settings, retains the reviewed mapping with the originals and imports no setting it cannot verify. *Acceptance:* A browser journey: on an operators-only board the submit form is absent and a widget or API submission answers 403, while voting and commenting work; hiding vote totals removes them from the board, request page and public API; turning on the voter list shows display names only and the vote control states it; an anonymised board shows "Anonymous" on every public read while the operator page shows the requester; a Canny API fixture maps `isPrivate` and `privateComments` without inventing API fields; for each board the owner enters or confirms posting permission, vote-count visibility, voter visibility and anonymity from the Canny dashboard and explicitly reviews comment participation; a board confirmed as posting off and votes hidden lands with both settings. The preview shows the source of each mapped setting, a changed mapping requires a fresh preview, and an unverified setting is not imported. Replay changes nothing; undo removes the imported settings, while a later native edit refuses reversal rather than overwriting it.

TRIAGE-001.was: Every request and inbox item can have one accountable owner; boards and themes have a default owner applied on capture; each operator has a queue of the items, requests and requester comments awaiting them. *Acceptance:* A captured item takes its board's default owner; reassignment moves it between queues; a queue lists only the operator's own items.

TRIAGE-004.summary: Restore internal note replies after their parent notes and retain complete private discussion.

NOTIFY-006 separately proves channel preferences and digests.

REL-014.summary: Schedule releases and status updates for a workspace-local time; Cron rechecks the publication conditions, publishes once, and keeps a failed entry as a draft with a durable author notice.
REL-014.was: A release (REL-002), an announcement (REL-018) or a status update (ROAD-008) can be scheduled for a time in `workspaceTimezone`. At that time Penny checks REL-002's conditions (REL-018's for an announcement or request target); if they fail, the release stays a draft and its author is notified. *Acceptance:* A clock-advanced test publishes a scheduled release once at its time; a release whose target is no longer Shipped stays draft and notifies its author.
REL-014.now: A release (REL-002), an announcement (REL-018) or a status update (ROAD-008) can be scheduled for a time in `workspaceTimezone`. Penny retains the UTC instant and the entered IANA timezone, shows the schedule and lets an operator cancel it before publication. At that time Penny checks the same current publication conditions as Publish now: REL-002's for roadmap targets, ROAD-008's for status updates, and REL-018's for announcements and request targets. If they fail, the entry stays a draft and its author receives a durable in-app failure notice. Scheduled publication is audited and repeated Cron runs publish the version only once. REL-018 inherits this scheduling, cancellation and failure behavior for announcements and request targets when those entry types ship. *Acceptance:* A clock-advanced test publishes a scheduled release and status update once at their times, never before; cancellation prevents publication; a release whose target is no longer Shipped and a status update whose approval is stale stay draft and notify their authors. The browser journey schedules and cancels through the release and status-update controls at both widths.

REL-018.summary: Name the scheduling, cancellation and failure rules announcements and request targets inherit from REL-014.
REL-018.was: An operator writes, labels (REL-015) and publishes a changelog entry with no target, as Canny's changelog allows: an announcement, for a fix, a small improvement nobody requested, or a pricing or policy notice. It needs a title, a body, a type or label and a publication date, publishes now or on schedule (REL-014) with no roadmap-state check, and has no outcome prompt (REL-008, REL-009) because it has no target. It appears on the changelog page, its feeds (REL-016) and the changelog widget (WIDGET-003). Its recipient snapshot (REL-004) is the updates subscribers (REL-012), narrowed by any segment send the operator chooses (REL-016); each receives it once under REL-006, REL-007 and NOTIFY-002, and unticking "Notify subscribers" (ticked by default) publishes it with no email. An operator can also link published requests to any release as request targets without a roadmap item: publication requires each linked request to be Shipped (REQ-016), unless the operator ticks "Mark linked requests Shipped", which sets each one through REQ-036 in the same transaction; each linked request's followers, vote-subscribed voters and subscribed author join the snapshot once, with that request as their context, and see its outcome prompt. Corrections follow REL-003. A release with a roadmap target still enforces REL-002. Today every release needs a roadmap target. *Acceptance:* A base and browser journey: an entry with no target publishes, appears on the changelog page, both feeds and the widget, and emails each updates subscriber once and nobody else; with Notify subscribers unticked it emails nobody; it shows no outcome prompt; a release whose roadmap target is Planned is still refused; a release with an Open request target is refused unless Mark linked requests Shipped is ticked, which makes the request Shipped and adds its subscribed voters to the snapshot once each.

NOTIFY-004.summary: Notification replies create no records through capture or provider-event routes.
NOTIFY-004.was: Notifications are sent from a no-reply address. A reply to any notification creates no evidence item, comment, request, or other record. The only inbound-mail route is CAP-009's dedicated capture address, which accepts mail only from operators and allowlisted senders and never from Penny's own notification addresses.
NOTIFY-004.now: Notifications are sent from a no-reply address. A reply to any notification creates no evidence item, comment, request, or other record. The only inbound-mail route is CAP-009's dedicated capture address, which accepts mail only from operators and allowlisted senders and never from Penny's own notification addresses. Penny reads no mail at any address it sends from: every notification, sign-in and verification message goes out from the deployment's `MAIL_FROM` or a NOTIFY-013 tested sender, carries `Auto-Submitted: auto-generated`, and has no reply-to unless the owner sets a monitored one under NOTIFY-013. The Worker has no mail handler and no route accepts a mail message. CAP-009 inherits the rest when it ships: its capture route refuses mail from Penny's own sender addresses, and its acceptance proves that a reply to a Penny notification creates nothing; NOTIFY-013 inherits keeping a configured reply-to off the capture address. *Status:* done (20 October 2026). `[NOTIFY-004]` in `tests/base/notifications.test.ts` sends a follower's status notification and checks its sender, absent reply-to and `Auto-Submitted` header, then posts its reply as a raw message, an Inbound Parse form and a JSON inbound webhook to the provider event route and each plausible capture path: every post is refused, and no table changes except the per-IP request counters every HTTP request charges.
